times. Nobody used the word that appears in the title of RFC 0002.

The survey was run once. It has not been repeated.

### A.8 Methodology and threats to validity

Self reported data for anything involving an individual session. Sensor
data for aggregate occupancy. Manual counting for queue depth. No
blinding. Single site. One operator for all home deployment measurements.
Small n for the airport, train, festival and camping environments, where
collection conditions were, in every sense, poor.

The direction of every finding is robust. The magnitude of any specific
number should be treated as illustrative. Nothing here should be cited
anywhere, by anyone, for any purpose.

## Appendix B: Configuration Reference

Complete reference for the client SDK. Every option, every default, every
regret.

### B.1 Connection

**`endpoint`** — `string`, required.

The target resource URI. Scheme is always `porcelain:`. Host is the
facility. Port is the stall.

No discovery mechanism is provided. Clients are expected to know where
they are going. In an unfamiliar building this is the single largest
source of latency and no library has ever solved it.

**`timeout`** — `number`, default `600000`.

Milliseconds before the client gives up. Ten minutes. The default was
chosen by measurement: sessions exceeding ten minutes with no progress
almost never complete, and persisting past it is the strain anti pattern
from RFC 0024 section 24.3.

Frequently overridden to `Infinity` by operators with a phone. The library
does not prevent this and ADR 004 says it should not.

**`retries`** — `number`, default `3`.

Attempts before escalation. Escalation means a different floor.

**`backoff`** — `'exponential' | 'linear' | 'none'`, default
`'exponential'`.

Base delay 30 seconds, multiplier 2, jitter mandatory. Jitter is not
optional and the library will throw at construction if you disable it,
because eleven engineers retrying at the top of the hour is the thundering
herd and it is entirely avoidable.

### B.2 Privacy

**`privacy`** — `boolean`, default `true`.

Never set this to `false`. There is no legitimate use case. It exists only
because a test suite needed it and removing it now would be a breaking
change to a package with one consumer, which is the reason every bad
option in every library still exists.

**`courtesy`** — `boolean`, default `true`.

Enables the mid session flush. Cover traffic. Protocol compliant under ADR
003 rather than merely polite, which is a distinction the documentation
makes carefully and no user has ever noticed.

**`cover`** — `'fan' | 'tap' | 'dryer' | 'none'`, default `'fan'`.

Acoustic countermeasure selection. Ranked in RFC 0006 section 6.3. `'fan'`
is broadband, continuous and plausible. `'tap'` is wasteful and legible.
`'dryer'` is bursty and therefore correlated with the signal it is meant to
mask, which makes it worse than nothing.

A fifth value, `'cough'`, was proposed and rejected on the grounds that it
is perfectly correlated with the payload and doubles the information
leaked. The PR is closed with a link to the padding oracle literature,
which is the single most over engineered code review comment in this
repository's history.

### B.3 Session

**`reading`** — `'phone' | 'book' | 'none'`, default `'phone'`.

The most consequential option in the library. Multiplies p99 duration by
roughly four. Increases satisfaction by an amount the team declined to
quantify.

Supported, permanently, per ADR 004. Warned about in capacity planning
documentation. Never deprecated. Contributors proposing its removal should
read section 37.4 first and consider whether they intend to police it.

**`posture`** — `'seated' | 'supported' | 'squat'`, default `'seated'`.

`'supported'` engages a footstool, approximating the squat anorectal angle
on seated hardware. Measurably better on transit time and required
pressure. Universally mocked until tried, then adopted permanently.

**`lock`** — `boolean`, default `true`.

Mandatory per ADR 006. Setting this to `false` logs a warning at
construction, a second warning at connect, and voids all support. The
warning text was written after an incident and has not been softened.

### B.4 Supply

**`preflight`** — `boolean`, default `true`.

Verifies the hard dependency before committing. Two seconds. The highest
expected value operation available anywhere in this document.

Default was `false` until v1.8.3. It was changed after the third support
ticket, all three of which described the same failure and none of which
used the same words.

**`reserve`** — `number`, default `1`.

Units of secondary supply required for preflight to pass. Setting this to
`0` means preflight passes on the last unit, which is technically true and
practically catastrophic.

### B.5 Environment

**`ventilation`** — `boolean`, default `false`.

Should be `true`. The default is `false` because the reference environment
is the home deployment, where it is usually unnecessary, and nobody
revisited the default when the office deployment shipped.

This is the most common configuration mistake in production and it is
entirely the library's fault.

**`lighting`** — `'continuous' | 'motion'`, default `'continuous'`.

`'motion'` requires a heartbeat. The client will emit one automatically if
configured, at 30 second intervals, which is the software equivalent of
the hand wave described in RFC 0009 section 9.3 and was added for exactly
that reason.

**`temperature`** — `number`, default `21`.

Degrees Celsius. Below 16 the operator's session duration rises measurably.
Below 10 the operator does not initiate a session at all, which is the
entire reason the indoor deployment superseded the outdoor one in v1.1.0.

### B.6 Observability

**`telemetry`** — `boolean`, default `false`.

Opt in, per ADR 005. When enabled, emits aggregate counts only, with no
identifiers, no timestamps finer than the hour, and no join key of any
kind. Aggregation happens before anything leaves the device.

The absence of a join key is the only real control in that list. The rest
are promises, and a promise is not a control.

**`onUrgency`** — `(level: number) => void`, optional.

Called on each change to the urgency level, 0 to 10. Register a handler
above 8 at minimum.

**`onPanic`** — `() => void | Promise<void>`, optional.

Called when the hard dependency fails after commitment. Must be registered
before `connect`. Registering it afterwards is the leading cause of
support tickets and the library cannot warn about it, because at
construction time it cannot know whether you intend to.

### B.7 Deprecated

**`stream`** — removed in v2.0.1.

Twenty three hours of availability. See RFC 0009 section 9.2. The option
name is reserved permanently and the library throws a descriptive error if
it is passed, which is more courtesy than the original release extended to
anyone.

**`shard`** — never shipped.

Proposed once. Rejected by ADR 001. The proposal is in the archive and the
review comments on it are the funniest thing in this repository, and they
are not reproduced here because two of the participants still work in the
building.

### B.8 Full example

```ts
const client = createClient({
  endpoint: 'porcelain://floor5:2',

  timeout: 600_000,
  retries: 3,
  backoff: 'exponential',

  privacy: true,
  courtesy: true,
  cover: 'fan',

  reading: 'phone',
  posture: 'supported',
  lock: true,

  preflight: true,
  reserve: 1,

  ventilation: true,
  lighting: 'motion',
  temperature: 21,

  telemetry: false,

  onUrgency: (level) => {
    if (level >= 8) logger.warn({ level }, 'escalating')
  },
  onPanic: async () => {
    await neighbour.request('assistance')
  },
})
```

Note `endpoint: 'porcelain://floor5:2'` rather than floor 3. This is the
single most valuable line in the entire configuration and it is knowledge
that took the author two years to acquire and one line to write down.
